records.summary:
This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which found no division-specific legal, incident or enforcement signal: its 2024 share of national LGBTIQ+ discrimination cases was 1.56% (Movilh regional table). Its recorded case trend follows the national one, which rose in 2025 to a record; a low share is not evidence of safety — most regions outside the two biggest rose that year.

There is no region-specific legal, incident or enforcement finding for this division; its recorded profile comes from the shared national case table. National frame: 2025 produced a record 3,620 discrimination cases on grounds of sexual orientation, gender identity or expression (+27.1%; 23% of all cases in 24 years), and 2024 was the first regression since the return of democracy. Protective national framework (Gender Identity Law 21.120 in force 2019, same-sex marriage 2022, anti-discrimination law 21.220) sits against concrete 2025-26 rollback (PAIG excluded from the 2026 budget; health-ministry circular N8 restricting PAIG for minors; legislative initiative CEI-57) and administrative document friction from Registro Civil identification-system issuance failures (Comptroller Final Report 264/2025), which is directly relevant to a traveller whose documents must match presentation.

records.name: Meta
records.summary:
No Meta-specific law, enforcement practice or incident finding for trans people appears in the record's surviving sources. The national reporting they carry frames what a visitor stands under anywhere in the country: an international broadcaster (August 2025) covered a wave of anti-LGBTQ attacks in Colombia through the killing of Sara Millerey, a trans woman beaten and killed in a northern metropolitan area, alongside attacks on same-sex couples, framing a rising national pattern of violence; and an international daily's investigation (July 2024) documented armed groups in a southern department circulating 'social cleansing' flyers against trans women and forcing them from their homes, with dozens killed nationally.

Those reports concern other departments. Nothing here marks Meta as materially safer or more dangerous than that national picture; armed-group presence in parts of Meta's territory makes the displacement dynamic the 2024 investigation describes plausible rather than remote, and the absence of Meta-specific findings is weak evidence of safety, not proof of it.
